327.speaker: Albin Clavin
327.text: "Next, it's time to talk about our election prospects."

328.speaker: Narrator
328.text: There was a sharp, soft knock on the door.

329.speaker: Albin Clavin
329.text: "I hope it's all right with you that I've invited Mr. Galade to this portion of the meeting."

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "How are you two getting along these days?"

333.speaker: Narrator
333.text: Albin went to get the door. Lucian walked in.

334.speaker: Albin Clavin
334.text: "He's a hard man to read. But I think we've made our peace."

335.speaker: Albin Clavin
335.text: "I don't know. Just a feeling. I'll let him in."

337.speaker: Narrator
337.text: If Lucian still resented my choice of Vice President, he didn't show it. His tone was nothing but cordial and professional.

338.speaker: Narrator
338.text: The three of us sat down. Albin handed out a new set of documents.

339.speaker: Lucian Galade
339.text: "Mr. Clavin, I'll let you take the lead on this."

341.speaker: Albin Clavin
341.text: "I've just received the results of a voter poll commissioned by Petr Vectern shortly before his, uh, departure."

345.speaker: Narrator
345.text: Lucian and I avoided looking at each other.

350.speaker: Albin Clavin
350.text: "It's okay, but not amazing. We shouldn't take it for granted that we'll win this election."

354.speaker: Albin Clavin
354.text: "It's looking good. Very good. The USP stands to increase its share of the vote by up to 20 percent compared to last time around."

355.speaker: Albin Clavin
355.text: "It's not great. Bad, even. The USP stands to lose up to 20 percent of the vote compared to last time around."

356.speaker: Player
356.text: "Excellent news. We no longer have to pander to voter interests."

358.speaker: Player
358.text: "I knew it! Another term for us, then."

359.speaker: Albin Clavin
359.text: "Well, we've still got a year to go. Anything could happen."

360.speaker: Albin Clavin
360.text: "That could still increase if we play our cards right. But it's already quite a healthy lead."

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "Good thing we don't need voters to win the election."

363.speaker: Player
363.text: "I'm not worried. We've still got time to win them over."

364.speaker: Player
364.text: "Tell it to me straight. Do we still have a chance?"

368.speaker: Albin Clavin
368.text: "Sordland is still a democracy, Mr. President. At least on paper."

370.speaker: Albin Clavin
370.text: "A year isn't a very long time, Mr. President."

371.speaker: Albin Clavin
371.text: "We still have a year to gain more votes. But we've got to think strategically."

372.speaker: Albin Clavin
372.text: "But yes, we can definitely gain more votes if we think strategically."

374.speaker: Lucian Galade
374.text: "There's no harm in striving for more."

375.speaker: Lucian Galade
375.text: "Which, presumably, is why you have retained the services of your chief strategist."

376.speaker: Player
376.text: "Lucian, are you still sore about this? Let it go."

377.speaker: Player
377.text: "Do you have something to add, Lucian?"

379.speaker: Lucian Galade
379.text: "I assure you I have. I fully trust Mr. Clavin's capabilities."

385.speaker: Albin Clavin
385.text: "You're doing better than ever with conservatives. We have nearly 100 percent of their support."

389.speaker: Albin Clavin
389.text: "You're doing reasonably well among conservatives. About two-thirds of them are likely to vote for you."

390.speaker: Albin Clavin
390.text: "Our support among conservatives has plummeted. We can no longer count on their vote at all."

391.speaker: Albin Clavin
391.text: "You've fallen out of favor with conservatives. Less than half of them are likely to vote for you."

395.speaker: Albin Clavin
395.text: "Looking at the demographics of the voters polled..."

402.speaker: Albin Clavin
402.text: "The liberal base appears divided, but you do have a considerable number of supporters there."

403.speaker: Albin Clavin
403.text: "Fortunately, your popularity among liberals has skyrocketed. You're on track to take a sizeable number of votes away from the PFJP."

404.speaker: Albin Clavin
404.text: "Unfortunately, you have next to no support from liberals."

411.speaker: Albin Clavin
411.text: "For better or worse, you certainly aren't popular with nationalists."

412.speaker: Albin Clavin
412.text: "For better or worse, most nationalists appear on track to vote for you."

413.speaker: Albin Clavin
413.text: "For better or worse, quite a few nationalists appear on track to vote for you."

420.speaker: Albin Clavin
420.text: "If you ever had any support from socialists, you've completely lost it now."

421.speaker: Albin Clavin
421.text: "The socialist left is divided nearly in half in its support for you."

422.speaker: Albin Clavin
422.text: "You've won over many fans on the left. The socialists are on your side."

426.speaker: Albin Clavin
426.text: "We're seeing some support from the Bludish community, but your popularity with them could definitely be higher."

430.speaker: Albin Clavin
430.text: "Good news: you're set to have the highest share of the Bludish vote of any Sordish president. You're even winning them away from the WPB."

431.speaker: Albin Clavin
431.text: "Unsurprisingly, none of the Bludish poll respondents said they were planning on voting for you."

435.speaker: Albin Clavin
435.text: "Lastly, we can't expect votes from centrists and unaffiliated voters unless we do something to win them over."

439.speaker: Albin Clavin
439.text: "Lastly, we're pulling a big share of the centrist and unaffiliated vote."

440.speaker: Albin Clavin
440.text: "Lastly, centrist and unaffiliated voters appear to be leaning in our direction."

441.speaker: Player
441.text: "So... I should just keep doing what I've been doing, then."

451.speaker: Albin Clavin
451.text: "If you want to play it safe."

453.speaker: Albin Clavin
453.text: "Look, I've spent half my career trying to discern the needs of liberal voters. I can advise you in that direction, if you want."

456.speaker: Player
456.text: "No, I don't need advice from either of you. I'll win the election my way."

460.speaker: Player
460.text: "No, it's pointless. I'm just going to lose. This meeting is over."

461.speaker: Narrator
461.text: Lucian smiled and bowed his head slightly.

463.speaker: Lucian Galade
463.text: "This may sound like common sense, but a convincing enough campaign can succeed where policies fail."

467.speaker: Lucian Galade
467.text: "Choosing to focus on your campaign was already a good start. I'd advise you to seize every chance for exposure that you can."

468.speaker: Lucian Galade
468.text: "Even if you've opted not to focus on your campaign at the moment, I'd still advise you to seize every chance for exposure that you can."

472.speaker: Player
472.text: "Oh. So I should do that television ad after all, then."

474.speaker: Albin Clavin
474.text: "All right, I'll notify the film crew."

479.speaker: Player
479.text: "I'm a man of substance, Lucian. Image means nothing to me."

481.speaker: Player
481.text: "I'd rather be signing bills than kissing babies."

482.speaker: Lucian Galade
482.text: "Perhaps, but we've both been in this game long enough to know how it is played."

485.speaker: Lucian Galade
485.text: "There is a not-insignificant portion of undecided voters who don't care who occupies the Maroon Palace as long as the economy is running smoothly."

489.speaker: Lucian Galade
489.text: "Mr. Holl's new plan could be key to winning them over. We must march towards a strong recovery."

490.speaker: Lucian Galade
490.text: "A robust economy such as the one we have now could make up for a multitude of unpopular policies."

494.speaker: Lucian Galade
494.text: "Propping up the economy just ahead of the election is a surefire way to win them over."
494.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn07_Results_Focus_Economy"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Economy"] >= 8) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Economy"] > 7) == false)

500.speaker: Albin Clavin
500.text: "I will say the liberal base is very concerned with equality. If you want their vote, you need rock-solid policies on women's rights and human rights in general."

506.speaker: Albin Clavin
506.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_MarketEconomy"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Archetype_CapitalistRayne"] == false)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Economy"] < 9) == false

507.speaker: Albin Clavin
507.text: "Liberals love a free market, so if you're anything less than a full-bore capitalist you're going to have to whip Sordland's economy into the best shape it's ever been."
507.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_ExcellentWomenRights"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_ExpandedHumanRights"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_MarketEconomy"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Archetype_CapitalistRayne"] == false)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Economy"] < 9)

1305.speaker: Lucian Galade
1305.text: "You already know I wasn't entirely supportive of your cooperation with Chief Justice Hawker..."

1309.speaker: Lucian Galade
1309.text: "However, in light of the current situation, I highly advise you to extend the state of emergency. That is the only way we can come out of this election intact."

1310.speaker: Lucian Galade

1318.speaker: Lucian Galade
1318.text: "...And as you know the state of emergency is about to expire soon. I have to *insist* not to extend the state of emergency any longer."

1319.speaker: Lucian Galade
1319.text: "...And as you know the state of emergency is about to expire soon. As much as I don't want to play into Mr. Hawker's hands, you *must* extend the state of emergency."

1323.speaker: Lucian Galade
1323.text: "...And as you know the state of emergency is about to expire soon. I have to *insist* not to extend the state of emergency any longer. That is the only way we can come out of this election intact."

1324.speaker: Lucian Galade
1324.text: "The polls may look promising but let's not forget that the Old Guards have too much influence on the agency which published these results. The numbers are surely skewed."

1325.speaker: Lucian Galade
1325.text: "We may not survive the elections if we enter elections in a state of emergency. The election would lose its legitimacy."

1326.speaker: Lucian Galade
1326.text: "I have reasons to suspect they will put you on trial if you back off now."

1327.speaker: Lucian Galade
1327.text: "We are too deep into this that we cannot back down now. Otherwise, elections will be the last of your worries."

1328.speaker: Lucian Galade
1328.text: "The polls may not look promising but the main reason of this is the state of emergency. We can still turn this around."

1329.speaker: Lucian Galade
1329.text: "Some people will surely raise their concerns about holding elections during an emergency. However, as long as we have our core support, nothing really matters."

1330.speaker: Lucian Galade
1330.text: "We will have our full control over the polling stations and the High Election Council. This means, we will not lose."

1331.speaker: Lucian Galade
1331.text: "Actually... There is one more thing, sir."

1333.speaker: Player
1333.text: "That sounds a little too much, Lucian. I'm thinking about not extending the emergency any longer."

1335.speaker: Lucian Galade
1335.text: "We would most likely win, sir. With all the power of the emergency, I will make sure to guarantee a victory."

1338.speaker: Lucian Galade
1338.text: "Anyway, I will not take more of your time. I hope you listen to my advice, sir."

1339.speaker: Player
1339.text: "What do you know about their plans?"

1340.speaker: Lucian Galade
1340.text: "Only that they have the authority to impeach you if you try something now."

1343.speaker: Player
1343.text: "I don't care anymore, Lucian. I'm thinking about extending the emergency again."
